title: Staged patches & compatibility gate: intake and prioritization for air-gapped on‑prem upgrade requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers have submitted requests for help coordinating OS/infra/package upgrades for Redwood Private installs that are fully air-gapped or have tightly scheduled egress windows. These requests vary (some ask for signed offline patch bundles, some for stepwise rolling upgrades integrated with WSUS/SCCM, others request assistance building a customer-hosted package mirror). Goal: define a staged-upgrade gating policy and an intake/prioritization rubric that lets PMs and SREs classify requests, provide a repeatable engineering scope template, and deliver a minimal, secure artifact distribution path for air-gapped customers.

Scope: this ticket defines the product decision, acceptance criteria, and intake scoring. Implementation (ENG work) will be tracked separately. Key constraints: no outbound connectivity allowed for some customers, signed and reproducible artifacts required, limited maintenance windows (often <4 hours), heterogenous OS/package managers (apt/yum/zip/nuget/Windows MSI via SCCM), customers may require FIPS/KMS integration.

High-level proposal: 1) Surface a new intake category "Airgap Upgrade Assistance" in the Customer Request form with structured fields (current runtime, OS distro + versions, existing package mirror approach, maintenance windows, required rollback window, compliance needs). 2) Create a staged-patch artifact format: containerized patch bundle + manifest (SHA256, signature), signed by Redwood, and a lightweight offline installer that supports pre-checksum validation and deterministic rollback. 3) Introduce a compatibility gate matrix that maps our runtime versions to supported OS/minor versions and notes known manual steps (kernel modules, firewall rules, kernel headers). 4) Define prioritization rubric: customer criticality, security exposure (CVE window), upgrade complexity, and required engineering effort. 5) Provide two delivery tracks: Standard Template (configurable, supported with runbook) and Eng Assisted (custom engineering and patch builds).
updates: 2025-02-15: Initial intake. Logged three large enterprise requests (one manufacturing air-gapped, one financial with FIPS requirement, one telecom with restricted egress windows). PM triage session held—Asha, Liam, Priya from Security attended.

2025-02-19: Drafted intake form fields and scoring rubric. Decided to require explicit OS + package manager and maintenance window fields to avoid back-and-forth. Action: convert draft to Zendesk/trait form component and surface in account portal (frontend work).

2025-02-24: Security review prelim notes: must sign artifacts with customer-verifiable key, support customer uploading their own key for verification in high-compliance cases. Security flagged requirement for reproducible builds. Action: /security to confirm KMS/HSM process with ENG-8840.

2025-02-28: Eng sync with serving/runtime and packaging teams. ENG-7321 scoped a minimal offline bundle prototype (signed tarball + manifest verifier). Trade-off: building a full package mirror automation vs shipping a one-off signed bundle per release. Decision: start with signed bundles (lower lift) and roadmap mirror tooling for Q3.

2025-03-03: Customer success provided customers' preferred windows and confirmed they will pilot the 'Standard Template' track for two customers. Need to prepare runbook checklist and rollback playbook. Liam to create runbook skeleton and identify required telemetry metrics to validate during the maintenance window.

2025-03-04: PM review: acceptance criteria refined; added due date 2025-04-01 for final intake form and scoring rubric. Next: finalize artifact format, draft runbook, and schedule internal demo with SRE and Security week of 2025-03-10.
acceptance_criteria: An intake form is implemented in the customer request workflow with required structured fields (OS + version, package manager, maintenance window, rollback requirements, egress constraints).
A documented prioritization rubric (customer criticality, CVE exposure, complexity, SLAs) is published and used to assign requests to Standard Template vs Eng Assisted tracks.
Signed offline patch bundle format is specified with a manifest schema and validation steps; prototype bundle proof-of-concept exists (ENG prototype PR linked).
Runbook for Standard Template upgrades (prechecks, validation, rollback) is drafted and reviewed by SRE and Security.
Customer success team confirms two pilot customers and a scheduled pilot maintenance window; telemetry checklist to validate success is agreed.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: fast, one-off signed bundles reduce time-to-delivery but increase per-customer maintenance; full mirror automation is higher engineering cost but scales better. We prioritize low-lift path to unblock customers and revisit automation after pilots.

Edge cases to capture in compatibility matrix: custom kernel patches, customers that forbid any outbound digital signatures (require physical key exchange), and Windows environments that mandate SCCM import steps. These will be handled in Eng Assisted track.
Follow-ups: Liam to sync with ENG-7321 and ENG-8840 to finalize manifest schema; Asha to coordinate pilot comms and legal for custom signing agreements.
